findings.title: Retry increments can be lost when cron runs overlap
findings.body: This writes a value derived from the reminder snapshot fetched earlier rather than atomically incrementing the database value. If two cron invocations process the same failed reminder concurrently, both can read `retryCount = 0` and write `1`; repeated overlaps can prevent the count from reaching the `gt: 1` cleanup threshold, so persistently failing reminders are not reliably deleted after two failures. Use an atomic increment (and consider preventing concurrent processing of the same reminder).
